enabled.title: Enable drag-and-drop path insertion
enabled.description: Master switch. When off, dragging a file or folder onto a terminal, editor or notebook does nothing.

pathType.title: Path type
pathType.description: Insert paths relative to the terminal's working directory or to the open document's folder. Absolute paths always work; relative paths in a terminal need the extension's server component, and where it is unavailable nothing is inserted rather than a wrong path.

pythonPathStyle.title: Python path style
pythonPathStyle.description: How a path is inserted into a Python file or notebook code cell: 'posix' inserts a quoted path string, 'pathlib' inserts a pathlib constructor expression.

pathlibConstructor.title: Pathlib constructor
pathlibConstructor.description: The constructor used when Python path style is pathlib. Choose Path only in files that already do `from pathlib import Path` - the extension inserts the expression, never the import.

terminalSeparator.title: Terminal separator for several paths
terminalSeparator.description: What separates several dropped paths in a terminal. 'space' puts them on one line, as arguments to whatever is already typed. 'newline' gives each path a line of its own, ending every line but the last with a backslash so the shell reads it as a continuation: nothing runs until you press Enter. Type the command before you drop - in bash only the last line can still be edited after a newline drop, so a command typed at the front of it runs the first dropped path instead; zsh keeps the whole buffer editable.

terminalQuotePaths.title: Quote paths in the terminal
terminalQuotePaths.description: Wrap each terminal path in single quotes instead of backslash-escaping the characters that need it. Both forms reach the shell as one argument per path, and quoting is the easier of the two to edit by hand afterwards.
